title: Google Ads Keywords for Accountants: Lists and Negatives

facts.fact: Responsive search ads take up to 15 headlines of 30 characters each, according to the page.
facts.quote: A responsive search ad takes up to 15 headlines of 30 characters each, which is enough to write service-specific copy for every ad group below.

facts.fact: Google's own help says negative keywords do not match close variants, so plurals and misspellings of each negative must be added manually.
facts.quote: Google’s own help says negative keywords don’t match close variants, so plurals and misspellings of every negative have to be added by hand.

facts.fact: The Uniform Accountancy Act, a model law that state accountancy laws largely follow, reserves the titles "certified public accountant" and "CPA" for licensees.
facts.quote: The Uniform Accountancy Act, the model law that state accountancy laws largely follow, reserves the titles “certified public accountant” and “CPA” for licensees

facts.fact: The Uniform Accountancy Act bars firms without a CPA firm permit from providing attest services, so audit keyword lists should be used only by licensed CPA firms.
facts.quote: The Uniform Accountancy Act, the model most state accountancy laws follow, bars firms without a CPA firm permit from providing attest services

facts.fact: A responsive search ad can hold up to 15 headlines of up to 30 characters each, according to Google's support documentation as cited by the page.
facts.quote: A responsive search ad can hold [up to 15 headlines of up to 30 characters]

facts.fact: The page recommends that a good ad group contain five to fifteen tightly related keywords.
facts.quote: A good ad group has five to fifteen tightly related keywords

facts.fact: The page says six ad groups cover most small and mid-size accounting practices.
facts.quote: These six cover most small and mid-size practices.

facts.fact: The page suggests starting an accounting firm's negative keyword list with about 60 terms, before plurals and misspellings are added.
facts.quote: Start with the six groups above, about 60 terms before plurals and misspellings, and add new ones from the search terms report weekly.

facts.fact: The page recommends checking the search terms report daily during the first two weeks of tax season.
facts.quote: In tax season, check daily for the first two weeks.

facts.fact: In WordStream and LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks, the Finance and Insurance category had a median cost per click of $3.39, the closest category the page cites to accounting.
facts.quote: the closest, Finance and Insurance, had a median cost per click of $3.39 and a 2.64% conversion rate

facts.fact: In WordStream and LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks, the Finance and Insurance category had a conversion rate of 2.64%, the lowest of 23 industries.
facts.quote: a median cost per click of $3.39 and a 2.64% conversion rate, the lowest of 23 industries

facts.fact: Tax services and financial planning services are Local Services Ads categories in the United States, which charge when a customer contacts the business rather than per click.
facts.quote: Tax services and financial planning services are [Local Services Ads categories in the US]

facts.fact: General accounting and bookkeeping are not listed as their own Local Services Ads category on Google's page, so keyword campaigns remain the main ad route for bookkeeping, payroll, CFO and audit work.
facts.quote: General accounting and bookkeeping are not listed as their own category on that page.

facts.fact: The Uniform Accountancy Act, published by the AICPA and NASBA as a model for state accountancy laws, reserves the titles "certified public accountant" and "CPA" for certificate holders.
facts.quote: reserves the titles “certified public accountant” and “CPA” for certificate holders

facts.fact: Per the page's FAQ summary of the Uniform Accountancy Act, the model reserves "certified public accountant", "CPA" and "public accountant", and bars titles likely to be confused with them, such as "certified accountant", "licensed accountant" and "registered accountant".
facts.quote: It reserves “certified public accountant”, “CPA” and “public accountant”, and bars titles likely to be confused with them

facts.fact: Google's trademark policy, as described on the page, says it does not restrict trademarks used as keywords, although trademarks in ad text can be restricted.
facts.quote: says it does not restrict trademarks used as keywords, but trademarks in ad text can be restricted
